page.layout: One page of text, one column. No marginal notes. Faint mirrored text at the lower left is show-through from the other side and is left out.

main_text.p: thaginem, contenti ostentatione infulatione que superba in portum reverte-runt. Hucusque Appiani verba Latinè reddita. Post quæ dicit, tertio ab hoc eventu die exisse rursum classem Puni-cam, & tunc navale prælium commis-sum esse difficillimum & pertinacissi-mum, fortunaque varium. In cujus prælii descriptione docet,aggerem fuisse ante mœnia Carthaginis spaciofum, portui vicinum, dudum ad excipiendas negotiatorum sarcinas excitatum: & juxta hunc, ne ponendis illic castris (cui rei ob spacium non incommodus erat) à Romanis occuparetur, murum breuem durante hoc bello esse extructum: hunc aggerem,quòd infestando portui, & oppugnandis mœnibus idoneus videretur; post certamen navale ad eundem in multam noctem extractum, à Scipione summâ vi postridiè esse appeticum, & in potestatem redactum, mox etiam collocatis ibi machinis variis vim munitionibus urbanis ex eo loco intentari cæpisse: Situm porrò ejus talem fuisse, ut obsessis accessus ad eum ad incendendas hostium machinas urbi perquàm periculosas (cujus rei defide-[?]rio vehementer æstuabant) nec terrâ (transitus enim non patebat) nec navi-vium, (erat enim mare ibi vadosum navium,)

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse side at the lower left (fragments such as "no", "non nonnor") is omitted. The word "appeticum" appears as printed; it is likely a printing error for "appetitum", left unchanged. The line "defide-rio" is read from a hyphenated line end and is uncertain. The final words "vium," and "navium" are reconstructed from the split word "navi-" / "vium" and should be checked against the scan. Long s is written as s throughout. The initial "thaginem" is a fragment from the previous page and stays as a fragment.
